newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SPANISH MIDFIELDERS OUTCLASS SLOVAKIA IN SECOND HALF.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPANISH MIDFIELDERS OUTCLASS SLOVAKIA IN SECOND HALF.

text.p: Midfielders Raul Gonzalez and Luis Enrique Martinez performed strongly in the second half to lead Spain to a comfortable 4-1 win over Slovakia in a World Cup qualifying match on Wednesday.
The result left Spain third in European group six with two wins and a draw. They are two points behind Slovakia and five behind Yugoslavia, who have won all their four games.
A surprisingly open game began with chances at both ends.

Julen Guerrero failed to finish off a well-worked move by the Spaniards with just six minutes on the clock, while both Tibor Jankula and Jaroslav Timko squandered chances after sloppiness in the Spanish defence.

Spain took the lead through Barcelona striker Juan Pizzi, who celebrated his return to the Tenerife stadium where he had become Europe's leading scorer by tapping home at the end of a move by Guerrero and Luis Enrique.
But Slovakia went in at the break level thanks to a well-struck free-kick by midfielder Dusan Tittel which left goalkeeper Andoni Zubizarreta floundering.
The visitors, without top striker Peter Dubovsky and veteran midfielder Lubor Moravcik through injury, were unable to respond in the second half as the Spanish midfielders pulled out the stops.
Spain took the lead again immediately after the break when Guillermo Amor finished off a fine move and Luis Enrique made it 3-1 with a curling shot 10 minutes later.

Alexander Vencel made some superb saves from Guerrero and Josep Guardiola as Spain looked set to run riot. But the Slovak goalkeeper was guilty of a serious error in the 61st minute when he let a long-range shot from Fernando Hierro through his legs.
Vencel made amends in the closing minutes by pushing a cheeky lob from Raul over the bar, denying the teenager the perfect end to his second international appearance.

"We've got to work and think about the very important game with Yugoslavia in a month's time," said Raul, who played with the maturity that characterises his performances for Real Madrid. "I'm only 19 and I have a lot to learn."
